articles.title: ATP Finals tennis: Carlos Alcaraz v Ben Shelton – live semi-final updates
articles.summary: ATP Finals updates from the last four in Turin Mail Katy | Men’s $350m prize money boost. So who wins today? Well, so much depends on Alcaraz’s physical condition. If his hamstring doesn’t hinder him, he should win, given the heights he’s hit this week and during the past two months.
body: The last time these two played a deciding set tie-break was in that New York classic two months ago. But Alcaraz still has his service game to get through, which given the way the serving script has gone in this set will probably go by in the blink of an eye … and it does, with Alcaraz conceding only one point. Tie-break time it is!

A serve-volley combo from Shelton gives the American 30-15. Shelton then surges forward to the short ball … but cracks his forehand into the net! 30-all. A huge point. Will it be break point, which could leave Alcaraz serving for the match, or game point? Game point, because Shelton does tremendously well to dig out a low volley before turning into Pete Sampras with a slam dunk! And 40-30 rapidly becomes game. Shelton has got himself at least a tie-break.

Alcaraz, now serving to stay in this semi-final with no margin for error, continues the trend here, whizzing through to love, though he can’t quite match Shelton’s ace count from the previous game, as he flashes down "just” two. Carlos, do better!

articles.title: Liverpool keeper Keating holds leaders Chelsea at bay in scoreless WSL draw
articles.summary: Khiara Keating’s resilient performance in goal denied Chelsea, the Women’s Super League leaders, and earned Liverpool a point. After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night, Chelsea drew a blank.
body: Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after beating City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the form of Aggie Beever-Jones, who scored her first WSL goal in more than a year in the 6-0 defeat of Charlton, have left Chelsea’s attack short.

Despite almost 70% possession and 47 touches in the box to Liverpool’s 12, Sonia Bompastor’s side amassed only 19 shots to Liverpool’s 13 and seven on target to their opponents’ four. Although the Blues remain unbeaten in the WSL, their third draw in five games in all competitions means City can leapfrog them at the top if they beat Tottenham on Sunday.
Liverpool had chances, particularly in the first half, but were hanging on after the break and Keating helped them to a fourth clean sheet, a tally bettered only by Bompastor’s side.

“It was a bit stressful; we don’t want to sit back but in games like this you have ‌to ride it out,” Keating told Sky Sports. “A clean sheet is ​always on our minds every game. We knew the mission. It was such a close game, it could have gone either way.”

articles.title: Ex-captain Moody joins England in emotional haka response
articles.summary: Former England captain Lewis Moody joins the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium.
body: Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) last year, stood at the centre of England's line-up - between captain Maro Itoje and one of the team's vice-captains, Ellis Genge - as they faced up to the traditional pre-match challenge.

Led by Genge's fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George, England then advanced to form a V shape, similar to the formation they took before last year's victory and the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final win against the All Blacks.
Moody, who was embraced by most of England's team in the aftermath of the challenge and its acceptance, also delivered the match ball.
With Twickenham energised, England started the match fast, with Henry Slade getting on the end of a Fin Smith grubber kick to score the first try after just four minutes.

articles.title: Championship roundup: Southampton get Larin lift as Norwich win five in a row
articles.summary: Southampton 2-0 Derby; Norwich 2-1 Cardiff. QPR get first away win since August at 10-man Millwall. Cyle Larin returned to action with a bang as Southampton extended their unbeaten run at home in the Championship to 18 games with a 2-0 victory over second-bottom Derby.
body: Larin turned in his eighth goal of the season but his first since 12 September – after a four-game drought and a hamstring problem. Divin Mubama added a second in stoppage time as Saints shrugged off worries of failing against lower-placed sides – having dropped points against Watford, Preston, Wrexham, Lincoln and Bolton already this season.

But for their four-point deduction for Spygate, the result would have taken Southampton top for at least a couple of hours. Derby would wind up bottom if Preston pulled off an unlikely win at West Ham.

Norwich came from behind to beat Cardiff 2-1 and make it five straight Championship victories – after losing their previous five. The Canaries went behind just after the break when Yousef Salech got on the end of a free-kick from deep but the visitors were quickly back on level terms as Paris Maghoma scored for the fourth game running.

Mathias Kvistgaarden then tapped home in the 68th minute after his penalty had been kept out by Nathan Trott. Ronan Kpakio had been penalised for bringing down Andre Brooks. Cardiff performed gamely all afternoon but were unable to get the equaliser their gutsy performance probably deserved.

articles.title: Elliot Anderson ends Manchester City’s losing run but boos greet Fulham draw
articles.summary: Manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four but at least ended their three-game losing run against Fulham. As they await the fate of their much-publicised appeal after being found guilty of financial breaches, their form has slumped as further evidenced by a…
body: Arguments will be made over Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal but City did not deserve anything more. The Norwegian uncharacteristically missed a number of fine chances as Rodrigo Muniz took advantage of City’s porous defence, who had to rely on Elliot Anderson to get anything out of the fixture.

City approached the game with the same subdued nature of the crowd, as is customary for a Saturday lunchtime kick-off. For a team amid a poor run of domestic form, they offered little in the way of dynamism from the off. A couple of half-chances were brushed off by Fulham, who were allowed to ease themselves into the game.

Confusion between defence and midfield has repeatedly caused problems for City under Enzo Maresca, who witnessed Marc Guéhi going over the halfway line to press a throw-in deep inside the Fulham half. When the visitors won the first header, the centre-back was out of position and everything was far too simple from then on. The former City winger Oscar Bobb shimmied and Muniz curled into the top corner from the edge of the box, before an emotional celebration in honour of his pregnant wife, who previously suffered a miscarriage.

articles.title: Liverpool frustrate Chelsea as Keating heroics leave WSL title race wide open
articles.summary: Liverpool frustrated Women's Super League leaders Chelsea with a stubborn defensive display to earn a goalless draw at the BrewDog Stadium leaving Manchester City with the opportunity to move top of the table.
body: Report and free match highlights as Liverpool frustrate WSL leaders Chelsea with a goalless draw; inspired goalkeeper Khiara Keating made seven saves to leave Manchester City with the chance to go top on Sunday.

Chelsea found it difficult to break down an inspired Khiara Keating and an outstanding Grace Fisk, with the goalkeeper making seven saves - her highest tally in a single game this season - as Sonia Bompastor's side dropped points for only the third time in their league campaign.
Chelsea, who arrived on Merseyside unbeaten in their previous 18 WSL matches, dominated possession for long periods but found Liverpool difficult to break down.

The hosts grew into the contest during the first half, with Beata Olsson, Cornelia Kapocs and Vivien Endemann causing problems, while Ceri Ramos went closest with an effort that narrowly cleared the crossbar. Keating was also called upon to deny Alyssa Thompson on the counter-attack as both sides went into the interval level.

articles.title: Lehmann again denies knowing about sandpaper plot
articles.summary: Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann says he and his staff did not encourage players to use sandpaper on the ball in 2018 despite detailed claims by Cameron Bancroft.
body: Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann has again vehemently denied any knowledge of the sandpaper plot, despite detailed allegations from Cameron Bancroft.

In an ongoing row about the cheating scandal that took place in Australia's third Test against South Africa in 2018, Bancroft published a testimony running to more than 4,000 words in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday.
At the same time, Lehmann was commentating on Australia's third one-day international against England, with Bancroft's account prompting him to leave the match early.
On Saturday, Lehmann returned to broadcast for the BBC and Australian network ABC on the first T20 international in Melbourne.

articles.title: Hickman breaks 16-year-old lap record in Macau win
articles.summary: Peter Hickman breaks the 16-year-old lap record for the Guia circuit in taking a fifth career win at the Macau motorcycle grand prix on Saturday.
body: It was a fifth triumph in the race for the 14-time Isle of Man TT winner and his first since 2023.
Hickman now sits third in the all-time winners' list at the event, behind nine-time victor Michael Rutter and Ron Haslam, who took six successes at the event.

The Lincolnshire rider dominated the race throughout after setting the pole position time in qualifying and had more than 38 seconds to spare over runner-up, Manxman Marcus Simpson, at the chequered flag.
Northern Ireland rider Paul Jordan completed the podium positions in third on his Jackson Racing Honda.

articles.title: NWSL, U.S. Soccer continue focus on women's soccer growth with player and executive development programs
articles.summary: The NWSL announced the creation of the player development rule on Thursday, as well as the Sporting Executive Leadership Program in conjunction with U.S. Soccer and FIFA
body: WASHINGTON, D.C. – The NWSL has always been a measuring stick for the growth of women's soccer in the U.S., which in recent years has been headlined by skyrocketing expansion fees and increased fan engagement. There's a buzzword that continues to pop up around the league, one that is rarely associated with the key performance indicators – pipeline. After she read out another list of attendance figures and viewership numbers before the 2026 season wraps up with Saturday's NWSL Championship (8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+ ), commissioner Jessica Berman made a hard pivot in her state of the league remarks on Thursday to say the league is officially in the business of prioritizing said pipeline.
